name: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge
authors: Tianhao Wu, Weizhe Yuan, Olga Golovneva, Jing Xu, Yuandong Tian, Jiantao Jiao, Jason Weston, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar (Meta FAIR; UC Berkeley; New York University). Lead affiliation: Meta FAIR (work led with UC Berkeley).
venue: EMNLP 2025 (main conference, pages 11537-11554, Suzhou, China; DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.583). Originally arXiv preprint 2407.19594 (July 28, 2024).
code_url: No official code/model release identified from the authors. The ICLR 2025 OpenReview submission certified no public GitHub/URL, and the paper does not announce a code release. Only community reimplementations of the predecessor Self-Rewarding exist (e.g., lucidrains/self-rewarding-lm-pytorch, Oxen-AI/Self-Rewarding-Language-Models).
reflection_type: learned-critic-model with a meta-level critic: the same model acts as judge (LLM-as-a-Judge scoring its own responses) and as meta-judge (LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge, judging its own judgements). The judging/meta-judging ability is itself improved by training, so it is a self-generated learned critic refined by a meta-critic rather than a separate frozen reward model.
feedback_source: self-generated. All three roles (actor, judge, meta-judge) are the SAME model; no external tool, unit test, human label, or ground-truth oracle is used for the training reward. A small human-derived seed (EFT data built from Open Assistant, used for SFT) bootstraps the judge. GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) is used only as an external evaluator/proxy at test time, never as a training signal.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine across training rounds within an Iterative DPO framework. Starting from an SFT (on EFT) seed of Llama-3-8B-Instruct, 4 iterations are run (M1->M2->M3->M4); each iteration generates on-policy responses, self-judges them, meta-judges the judgements, builds preference pairs, and trains the next model via DPO. (Iters 1-2 train BOTH actor and judge preference pairs; Iters 3-4 train actor pairs only.)
reflection_object: model weights are the persistent locus of improvement (via DPO). The proximate objects reflected on are two-fold: (1) the actor's output content / candidate responses (reflected on by the judge), and (2) the model's own reasoning-as-judge, i.e. the judgements themselves including their rubric scores (reflected on by the meta-judge). The key novelty over Self-Rewarding is reflecting on the judgement (the critique reasoning chain), not just the response.
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update. Self-generated preference data (response pairs + judgement pairs) is consumed by DPO to update the model's weights each iteration; there is no inference-time in-context reflection loop.
requires_training: DPO/preference (Iterative DPO). Each iteration constructs preference pairs from self-rewarding (actor) and meta-rewarding (judge) signals and runs DPO. Seeded by an SFT stage on the EFT (LLM-as-a-Judge) dataset; the actor is not re-trained on human responses because the seed is already instruction-tuned.
reward_or_critic_model: meta-judge plus self-as-judge: the policy model is its own judge (assigns 0-5 scores via an additive 5-criteria LLM-as-a-Judge rubric, averaging N=11 judgements) AND its own meta-judge (pairwise LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge comparing two judgements, with Elo/MLE scoring to derive meta-rewards). No separate trained reward model or external verifiable reward is used in the loop.
distillation_target: model-weights. Both the self-rewarding (response) signal and the meta-rewarding (judgement-quality) signal are distilled into the next iteration's parameters via DPO; no external memory, skill library, or persisted prompt/rule artifact is produced.
emergent_vs_engineered: scaffold-engineered: the actor/judge/meta-judge self-play loop, the LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge prompt, the length-control selection, and the Elo-based meta-reward are all explicitly engineered pipeline components, not RL-emergent reflective behavior. The improvement of the judging ability across iterations is an emergent training-dynamics effect within that engineered scaffold.
memory_type: none. No explicit episodic memory, scratchpad, or skill library. 'Memory' is implicit: experience is absorbed into model weights and into the per-iteration self-generated preference datasets.
memory_persistence: cross-task / cross-iteration: learning accumulates in weights across the 4 training rounds. There is no within-episode or cross-session inference-time memory store.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a for inference-time memory. At the data level, each iteration regenerates training data on-policy from the current model (sampling 5,000 of 20,000 seed prompts per iteration, K=7 responses, N=11 judgements per response) and SELECTS preference pairs via score-based selection with length-control (top/bottom quality tiers, parameter rho) for the actor and via meta-judge Elo ranking (highest vs lowest Elo judgement) with a verbosity length-filter for the judge. This is regenerate-and-select per round rather than append-only accumulation.
error_localization_granularity: response-level for the actor (a single averaged 0-5 score per whole candidate response; no step/token/block-level credit assignment) and judgement-level for the judge (the meta-judge does pairwise comparison of two whole judgements). Granularity is thus holistic at the response level and holistic at the critique level; no fine-grained intra-response error localization.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: an offline training procedure that improves the model across newly generated instruction-following prompts and iterations; it is not within-task in-context refinement of a single response at inference.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only / training-time improvement: there is no mid-trajectory recovery or post-hoc revision of a single answer at inference. The DPO loss pushes the policy away from lower-scored responses and the judge away from lower-quality (lower-Elo) judgements, improving future behavior via weight updates.
task_domains: general-alignment / instruction-following (primary). Also probes QA/reasoning-flavored categories within AlpacaEval (science, gaming, literature, etc.) and multi-turn dialogue (MT-Bench). Not applied to code, math benchmarks, web-navigation, or embodied tasks (math is one weak category).
benchmarks: AlpacaEval 2 (length-controlled win rate vs GPT-4-Turbo), Arena-Hard, MT-Bench (Turn 1 / Turn 2). Reward-modeling quality measured by judge agreement/Spearman correlation with GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) and with human rankings on a held-out Open Assistant split (190 samples / ~580 responses).
headline_result: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct with NO additional human data, 4 iterations of Meta-Rewarding raise AlpacaEval 2 length-controlled (LC) win rate from 22.92% (seed) to 39.44% (Iter 4), outperforming GPT-4-0314 and approaching Claude-Opus level; Arena-Hard score rises from 20.6% to 29.1% (+8.5). It beats both Self-Rewarding+length-control (35.49% LC) and SPPO (38.77% LC, which uses a reward model trained on human+GPT-4 data).
baselines: Seed Llama-3-8B-Instruct; SFT-on-EFT; Self-Rewarding LLM (Yuan et al., 2024c) equipped with the same length-control (the key ablation isolating the meta-judge contribution); SPPO (Wu et al., 2024) as a strong external-reward-model baseline; an external-reward-model variant using Starling-RM-34B; and GPT-4 / Claude-Opus as leaderboard reference points.
gains_vs_baseline: AlpacaEval 2 LC win rate: 22.92% (seed) -> Iter1 27.85% -> Iter2 32.66% -> Iter3 35.45% -> Iter4 39.44% (about +16.5 points over seed). Versus the strongest comparable baseline Self-Rewarding+LC: 35.49% (Iter4) vs 39.44%, i.e. ~+3.95 points attributable to the meta-judge. Versus SPPO 38.77% (which uses human+GPT-4 reward data): +0.67. Arena-Hard: 20.6% (seed) -> 29.1% (Iter4), +8.5; vs Self-Rewarding+LC Iter4 27.3%, ~+1.8. MT-Bench Turn 1: 8.319 -> 8.738 with <=0.1 drop in Turn 2 (Self-Rewarding+LC drops >0.2 in Turn 2 without improving Turn 1). Reward-modeling: judge agreement-without-ties with GPT-4 improves up to +12.34% (Self-Chosen Pairs, Iter 2) and >+6% (GPT-4-Chosen Pairs) over Self-Rewarding at matched iterations.
compute_cost_profile: Training-side only; no inference overhead at deployment (final model is a single standard 8B model). Per iteration on 5,000 prompts: actor samples K=7 responses (~35,000 responses) and judge generates N=11 judgements per response (~385,000 judgements), then meta-judge does pairwise battles on judgement pairs (each compared twice for positional debias) followed by Elo/MLE scoring, then DPO fine-tuning of the 8B model. 4 iterations total. Substantial generation/judging cost during data creation (N=11 judgements and O(N^2)-style judgement battles are the dominant cost); no GPU-hour/FLOP figure reported in the paper.
known_limitations: (1) The 5-point judging system produces frequent ties and saturates toward the maximum score as training progresses (scores drift to 4.5/4.75/4.9), making further improvement hard to detect; a more nuanced multi-aspect or comparison-based scoring is suggested. (2) Judge-training limitations: meta-judge positional bias persists despite debiasing and hindered further gains in Iteration 3; the judge develops a strong score-bias (prefers higher-score judgements ~97.7% by Iter 2), accelerating score saturation. (3) The judge shows limited improvement on NON-self-generated (out-of-distribution) responses, and its correlation with human rankings is not sustained over later iterations (distribution shift). (4) Length-bias requires explicit length-control mechanisms in both response and judgement selection. (5) Only evaluated up to 8B / 4 iterations on Open-Assistant-distribution prompts.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify / intrinsic-only for the training signal: rewards and meta-rewards come entirely from the model's own LLM-as-a-Judge and LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge with NO ground-truth oracle, external tool, or verifiable reward in the loop. A small human-derived EFT seed (Open Assistant ranked responses) bootstraps the judge in the SFT stage, and GPT-4 is used as an external evaluator at test time but not as a training signal. This is the 'self-verify without oracle labels' regime, distinct from oracle-dependent self-correction.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive within scope: unlike intrinsic single-shot self-correction (which degrades without oracle feedback), the self+meta judging signal drives genuine measured gains in BOTH instruction following (AlpacaEval LC 22.9%->39.4%) and judging quality (higher agreement with GPT-4 and human rankings) via weight updates. Efficacy is amplified specifically by training the JUDGE (the meta-judge contribution: +~4 LC points over Self-Rewarding+LC). However, gains are not unbounded: judge correlation with humans is not sustained in later iterations and score saturation/positional bias cap improvement (notably blocked further judge gains at Iteration 3).
calibration_effect: degrades / overconfident on the judging side (a documented 'judging-tax'): after training, the meta-judge almost always prefers higher-score judgements (63.0% Iter1 -> 97.7% Iter2) and the judge's score distribution concentrates toward the maximum (mean 4.1 -> 4.7+), reducing discriminative ability and reflecting score-bias and overconfidence. The paper does not report standard confidence-calibration metrics for the actor's answers, so actor-side calibration is not-measured; the judge-side miscalibration is explicitly analyzed as a limitation.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a: this is a training/self-improvement method, not a failure-attribution or trace-analysis object. It does not classify failure modes or attribute responsible agents/steps. (It does, however, analyze its own induced biases: judge score-bias and meta-judge positional bias.)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the saturation/reward-hacking failure mode of Self-Rewarding, where training only the actor while the judge stays static causes rapid saturation or overfitting to a non-improving reward (a form of 'superficial self-reflection' / reward-hacking in MAST-style terms). It explicitly co-trains the judge to keep the reward signal improving. It also surfaces and partially mitigates length-bias (verbosity reward hacking) and positional bias. It does not address multi-agent coordination failure modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new reusable benchmark or dataset released. Uses existing resources: the EFT seed data and 20,000 instruction prompts from Self-Rewarding (Yuan et al., 2024c) (originally generated by Llama-2-70B-Chat), Open Assistant for judge/reward-modeling evaluation, and AlpacaEval 2 / Arena-Hard / MT-Bench for actor evaluation. Self-generated preference datasets were not publicly released.
builds_on: Self-Rewarding Language Models (Yuan et al., 2024c, ICML 2024) — the direct predecessor it extends by adding the meta-judge; Iterative DPO (Xu et al., 2023, Pairwise Cringe Optimization); DPO (Rafailov et al., 2024); LLM-as-a-Judge / MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2024); RLHF/InstructGPT (Ouyang et al., 2022); RLAIF / Constitutional AI (Bai et al., 2022); length-bias mitigation work (Singhal et al., 2023; Dubois et al., 2024; Park et al., 2024; length-following Yuan et al., 2024b); Elo/MLE ranking from LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al., 2024). Seed model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct; SPPO (Wu et al., 2024) as a contemporaneous comparison.
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited as a foundational self-improvement / self-judging method in subsequent self-rewarding and label-free RLVR / self-alignment work and surveys (e.g., 'Sailing by the Stars: A Survey on Reward Models and Learning Strategies for Learning from Rewards', Wu 2025, arXiv 2505.02686; broader self-rewarding reasoning, CREAM consistency-regularized self-rewarding, Co-rewarding, and meta-judge / judge-training follow-ups). The meta-judge / judging-skill-training idea informs later work that trains the critic as well as the actor.
reasoning_model_native: no: predates and does not target o1/R1-style reasoning models with RL-emergent built-in reflection. It is an alignment / instruction-following self-improvement method on Llama-3-8B-Instruct; the reflection is an engineered LLM-as-a-Judge / LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge scaffold with chain-of-thought judgements, not RL-emergent reasoning. The meta-judge does elicit CoT reasoning in its critiques, but the model is a standard instruct model, not a reasoning model.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strong conceptual link to on-policy self-improvement / self-distillation: each iteration generates on-policy samples (responses and judgements) from the current model, self-scores them with its own (meta-)judge, and distills the resulting preference signal back into weights via DPO — a self-bootstrapping loop where the model is its own teacher and student. The distinctive twist is distilling improved JUDGING skill (critique quality), closely related to self-optimizing the critic/skill rather than only the policy. It is not classic teacher->student distillation (no external teacher).
sample_efficiency: 4 DPO iterations (M1->M4) reach the headline gains, with judge co-training active only in Iters 1-2; most actor gains continue through Iter 4 while judge-quality gains plateau / are blocked by Iteration 3 (positional bias, score saturation). Per iteration: 5,000 prompts, K=7 responses, N=11 judgements per response. Number of iterations to full saturation is not characterized; gains over Self-Rewarding are modest in absolute terms (~+4 LC points) but achieved without any added human data.
